label: rem:markov-axioms-primitive
title: Primitive Markov-trace axioms (M1–M4 from Jones 1985 / Wenzl 1988) in Lean; discharges the `MarkovDisjointStabilisation` class for `prop:categorical-chain-convergence-mechanisms`
html:
Let R be a commutative ring and q \in R^{\times} an invertible element with a chosen square root q^{1/2}. The Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M on the Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is the unique linear functional satisfying:

  1. Normalisation: \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1.
  2. Cyclicity: \mathrm{tr}_M(xy) = \mathrm{tr}_M(yx) for all x, y.
  3. Stabilisation by \sigma_n: \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_n(R, q), where z = q^3/(q^2+1) is the Markov-trace loop value (convention D; forced, see below).

Stabilisation by \sigma_n^{-1} — often listed as a fourth axiom — is not an independent condition. Substituting the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - (q - q^{-1}) into axiom 3 and using linearity of the trace (with x \cdot 1 = x) forces

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n^{-1}) \;=\; z_{-} \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x),
  \qquad
  z_{-} \;:=\; z - (q - q^{-1}),

so the negative-crossing loop value z_{-} differs from z whenever q \neq \pm 1. No choice of trace parameter makes the two stabilisations scale by mutually inverse factors either: z \cdot z_{-} = 1 has the sole solutions z = q and z = -q^{-1}, the one-dimensional characters of H_n(R, q), both of which are degenerate. Link invariance of the Jones polynomial is instead restored by the writhe prefactor outside the trace (Jones–Markov trace).

Axioms 1–2 with an unspecified stabilisation parameter admit a one-parameter family; axiom 3 selects one member of it, and which member is not free. The selection is forced by the dimension of the mass fibre:

  • lem:feynman-eigenbasis-decomposition already writes the row cap \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 into the mass channel's own decomposition — V is the fundamental of \mathrm{SU}_q(2), and the summand count \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 is the two-row count and no other. So y_{(1^3)} = 0 is a restatement of the decomposition the mass chapter uses, not an extra assumption.
  • Given y_{(1^3)} = 0, markovWeights_eq_jones_of_threeRow_eq_zero (MarkovTraceTLUniqueness.lean, sorry-free) shows the faithful normalised Markov trace is unique and equals z = q^3/(q^2+1) — convention D. The competing root z = q is real but degenerate (y_{(2,1)} = 0, not faithful on \mathrm{TL}_3), which is why the faithfulness hypothesis is load-bearing (markovWeights_degenerate_root).

So the loop value is a consequence of the fibre being two-dimensional, not a stipulation. Full forcing argument: 2026-08-08-mass-fibre-dimension-forces-convention-d.md; the D-vs-C analysis it rests on: 2026-08-08-borromean-trace-convention-forcing.md.

Convention D has y_{(1^3)} = 0, so it is the trace whose braid closure is the Jones polynomial: under D the "Jones–Markov" name is accurate, and under convention C — z = 1/(q^{1/2}+q^{-1/2}), where the loop value is stipulated rather than derived — it is not.

Because \mathrm{tr}_M is compatible with the tower inclusions and evaluates disjoint generators by iterated application of axiom 3, the joint Markov trace of two braids acting on disjoint strand sets is strictly multiplicative:

  \mathrm{tr}_M(K_1 \sqcup K_2) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(K_1) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(K_2).

Appending k further strands, each stabilised by one positive crossing, multiplies this value by z^k (one factor of z per application of axiom 3). This derives the inter-knot decoupling theorem from primitive Markov axioms.
